name: Stratiotosuchus
sum: Stratiotosuchus is an extinct baurusuchid crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous Adamantina Formation of Brazil, with one of the largest known baurusuchid skulls.
wsnote: The holotype skull is 47 cm long, among the largest of the group; no body length is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: A robust, laterally compressed skull 47 cm long from a mature individual; specimen number not given in the sources consulted.
material: The holotype skull, found in the 1980s and named in 2001, plus later referred material including a juvenile.
biology: Its ziphodont teeth (curved, serrated, laterally compressed) and robust skull suggest a hyperpredator that, like other baurusuchids, may have filled niches held by theropods elsewhere.
author: Campos et al. 2001

images.caption: Skeletal reconstruction of Stratiotosuchus beside a human silhouette.
